constraints_invoked.F1_loss_does_not_transfer: training-loss effects do not transfer to closed-loop success (1-step loss proxy passed while the fine-tune was the worst arm ever)
constraints_invoked.F4_seed_steers: same-seed weight updates 97% aligned across different draws; data fingerprint ~1.5%
constraints_invoked.F5_encoding: flow-matching loss gradient does NOT encode scene semantics/region (AUC 0.577 < 0.598 null floor) but DOES encode action quality (AUC 0.778)

TEST_A.signal: JEST / RHO-LOSS learnability: score(z) = L(z; pi_0) - L(z; reference), reference = a stronger retained pull checkpoint

A_i_execution_quality_axis.prediction: POSITIVE. Raw L(z; pi_0) separates style_lo (higher loss) from style_hi with AUC >= 0.70. The learnability DIFFERENCE score separates too but WEAKER than raw loss (AUC 0.55-0.70), because a stronger reference also has higher loss on inconsistent demos, so the quality component partially cancels in the difference.
A_i_execution_quality_axis.directional_claim: style_lo has HIGHER raw loss than style_hi at pi_0

A_ii_failure_region.prediction: NULL. AUC(in-region vs out-region) in [0.45, 0.60], i.e. at or below the Q0 shuffle-null floor of 0.598. Per F5 the loss does not see region membership; a scalar loss can only be weaker than the full gradient, which already failed the gate.

A_iii_pull_level_prediction.prediction_primary: NULL on content-only arms. Spearman(mean learnability of a pull's draw, realized delta) over pulls whose selection axis is NOT execution quality (null, random, tall, mid, easy, gradarm, gc, survivor) has |rho| < 0.30 with a bootstrap CI covering 0.
A_iii_pull_level_prediction.prediction_secondary_preregistered_confo: If the execution-quality arms (style_hi / style_lo / gradqual / planted_bad) are POOLED IN, a nonzero correlation MAY appear. That would be a QUALITY detector, not a learnability-to-outcome predictor, and must be reported as confounded: those arms were constructed on the quality axis, which F5 says the loss can see and which the style race showed moves rollouts.
A_iii_pull_level_prediction.rationale: F1 (loss does not transfer), F4 (seed dominates the update, data fingerprint ~1.5%), and the already-measured Q3 result (no pi_0-time statistic of a draw predicted delta, |rho|<=0.23 at n=16).
A_iii_pull_level_prediction.falsifier_of_null: |rho| >= 0.5 on content-only arms with CI excluding 0

TEST_A.stability_requirement: report SE of the per-demo score from M independent (noise,time) draws under common random numbers across checkpoints; declare the estimate stable only if SE(score) << between-demo SD(score).

TEST_B.signal: Graves/ODM learning-progress reward: held-out loss on a fixed slice at step 5000 vs at the final step; does early loss-progress predict the pull's realized rollout delta?
TEST_B.prediction: INVALID / NULL. Per F1 and F3, held-out-loss progress will NOT predict final realized delta on the content arms: |Spearman| < 0.30, and within-round paired sign agreement ~50% (chance).

preregistered_validity_criterion.VALID: Spearman(loss-progress, delta) >= 0.50 across non-catastrophic pulls AND within-round paired sign agreement >= 70%

TEST_B.prediction_resolution_floor: The reward may still have resolution for CATASTROPHIC corruptions (a -20pp planted-bad-style arm). If so the honest conclusion is: a learning-progress reward is a SAFETY FILTER, not an allocator - it cannot rank arms in the +/-3-8pp band where bandit decisions actually live.
TEST_B.why_this_is_the_decision: an online bandit on this stack is only possible if a sub-pull-cost reward ranks arms. Step-5000 held-out loss is the cheapest such reward that is not a 1.5k-step burst. If it fails, every remaining online design must use rollouts, i.e. 5-9 GPU-h per unit of feedback.
